status: Fixed in follow-up; original evidence retained
problem: Compression preview counts an output with a matching source stem as reusable even when runtime compression rejects its metadata or changed settings. Guided stage selection can omit the required compression work.
evidence: Python R01: change max_width after writing valid vmeta; preview will_skip=1 while _find_reusable returns no reusable path. Frontend stage omission follows from the preview contract; a live browser pipeline was not run.
recommendation: Share a read-only compression reuse predicate between preview and runtime, using source identity, metadata freshness, effective settings, probe validity and skip_existing/force policy.
acceptance: Preview and execution agree for changed settings/source, corrupt or missing output, duplicate basenames, skip_existing=false and force=true. Preview does not mutate artifacts.

status: Fixed in follow-up; original evidence retained
problem: Compression fingerprints and stored settings omit codec and effective CRF; changing those options can reuse an output encoded with old parameters.
evidence: Python R02: in CRF mode, changing both codec and CRF leaves the fingerprint and metadata matcher unchanged.
recommendation: Version the effective compression settings and reuse one serializer for metadata writing and matching. Include codec and mode-relevant CRF; retain safe legacy reads.
acceptance: Codec changes invalidate reuse; CRF changes invalidate CRF-mode reuse; irrelevant CRF changes in target-size mode do not. Legacy metadata remains readable with an explicit regeneration policy.

problem: Refine reads JSON before a long AI call and saves without an expected version, overwriting intervening editor changes. Busy check and claim are separate operations, and the flag is cleared before the final write.
evidence: Python R03: a provider callback performs a real versioned manual save; refine subsequently returns success and replaces it with the AI result. Existing backup behavior can retain recovery copies; this is not a claim that all history is destroyed.
recommendation: Capture the input content version and compare-and-swap on completion. Atomically claim refinement through commit; integrate project artifact concurrency and cancellation with managed tasks.
acceptance: A concurrent edit causes a clear 409 without replacing it; two refinements cannot both claim one file; cancellation/error releases ownership; the busy lifetime includes persistence. Normal refinement still succeeds.

problem: A delayed refinement response for video A unconditionally replaces the shared texts/voiceover buffer after the user switches to video B. The later render guard does not protect the data buffer.
evidence: Frontend R04: switch currentVideo to B before resolving refinement A; active state.texts becomes AI A. A subsequent B save could persist the wrong content; that later save was not performed by the probe.
recommendation: Bind response application to project, artifact, entity, editor revision and request generation. Store inactive results by artifact identity or require a fresh load, while preserving newer edits.
acceptance: Delayed A success/error cannot change B content, version, dirty flag or status. Switching projects or editing A while refinement runs also preserves current content. Returning to A loads its correct saved result.

problem: selectPlan lacks a request-generation guard. A slow earlier day request can replace the plan and preview mapping after a later day has already loaded.
evidence: Frontend R05: start day1 then day2, resolve day2 then day1; currentDay remains day2 while state.plan contains Day 1.
recommendation: Capture project/day/entity identity and a selection generation; apply both success and failure only for the current selection. Guard version and preview state together.
acceptance: Out-of-order loads, errors, project changes and plan-to-video navigation never replace the current plan or its media mapping/version; saving day2 cannot submit day1 data.

problem: Save generation changes only when another save starts. A successful pending save clears dirty even if the user made a newer edit or navigated to another editor while the request was running.
evidence: Frontend R06: submit a texts save, replace the buffer with a later dirty edit, then resolve success; the unsaved later content remains but dirty becomes false.
recommendation: Snapshot the submitted content and track edit revision plus full save-target identity. Clear dirty only if the active target/revision still equals the submitted revision; retain the returned version for the saved target.
acceptance: Edits during saves remain dirty for plan/texts/voiceover/config. Navigation and out-of-order saves do not clear another target's dirty state. Conflict handling preserves unsaved content.
dependency: Shared editor revision model useful for R04/R05

problem: Producers and artifact indexing support configurable subdirectories, but several Web readers still hard-code texts/scripts/compressed. Artifacts can exist or be listed yet be unreadable or unplayable.
location: clio/ui/services/file_service.py:615; clio/ui/services/file_service.py:626; clio/ui/handler_factory.py:449; clio/ui/routes/videos.py:214; clio/ui/routes/videos.py:741; clio/ui/routes/waveform.py:36; clio/config/models.py:649
evidence: Python R07: files under configured custom texts/scripts directories exist while Web resolvers return None. Hard-coded video/waveform roots were verified statically.
recommendation: Use configuration-aware artifact/media resolution in all route families, with existing legacy read-only fallbacks and containment checks.
acceptance: Default and nested custom subdirectories work across generation, listing, GET/PUT/refine, playback, metadata and waveform. Legacy artifacts remain readable and traversal/symlinks remain rejected.

problem: Texts/scripts resolution validates the basename but follows filesystem symlinks without the project's containment/symlink validation. A planted link can expose a file outside the artifact root to these route consumers.
evidence: Python R08: scripts/linked.json points outside the output root; resolve_in accepts and reads it, while validate_within_root rejects it. This requires a planted link and route access; no unauthenticated Internet exploit or arbitrary-write exploit is claimed.
recommendation: Validate the candidate's lexical path, resolved containment and symlink components through the existing shared policy before any read or write consumer uses it. Return a consistent forbidden response.
acceptance: Final and intermediate symlinks escaping the artifact root are rejected by GET/PUT/refine routes; ordinary artifacts and permitted legacy locations still work. Windows-capable and Unix tests exercise the same policy.

problem: Auto-copy copies only draft_content.json even though export emits draft_meta_info.json and subtitles.srt. A fresh destination lacks the generated discovery metadata; an existing destination can keep stale metadata.
evidence: Python R09: a three-file generated bundle becomes a one-file copied destination. Actual JianYing discovery/import was not tested, so universal app-level failure is not asserted.
recommendation: Define and copy the complete supported draft bundle, rewriting destination-dependent metadata and identifiers as needed; publish the bundle only after all files are ready.
acceptance: Fresh and existing destinations contain consistent content/metadata/subtitles with correct destination paths. Verify discoverability and import in the documented supported JianYing version and record that version.
dependency: Implement with R10; desktop import validation required

problem: Auto-copy uses the same vlog_export_<day> destination and replaces existing draft content without a destination overwrite gate or backup. Re-exporting can replace manual editing work; different projects with day1 share the same destination name.
evidence: Python R10: edit destination draft_content.json, export again, and observe replacement with no backup in the destination. Cross-project collision follows statically from the day-only name.
recommendation: Create a new project-scoped draft identity/directory by default. Explicit replacement must require confirmation and retain a recoverable complete backup; stage publication to handle failures.
acceptance: Repeat exports and two projects sharing day1 preserve prior manually edited drafts. Explicit confirmed replacement is recoverable. Failure/cancellation does not leave a half-published destination.

status: Fixed by credential retirement work; original evidence retained
problem: Provider TTL retirement respects active_calls, but explicit cache clearing closes active providers immediately. Configuration/environment saves call this path and can interrupt in-flight AI requests.
evidence: Python R11: within provider_use, cache clearing invokes provider.close before the active lease exits. A live network failure was not induced.
recommendation: Invalidate lookup entries immediately but retire active providers until their last lease exits. Separate graceful invalidation from explicit process shutdown and cover the provider acquisition-to-lease handoff.
acceptance: Saving config during an active provider call does not close that call's client; new calls use new settings; old clients close exactly once after all users exit, including exceptional exits.

problem: FileTokenUsageStore protects read-modify-write with an instance lock, but independent store instances target the same file. Atomic file replacement cannot prevent their lost updates.
evidence: Python R12: synchronize two independent writers after reading; both calls succeed but persisted history contains only one call.
recommendation: Serialize the entire transaction by canonical storage path across instances; use a file lock or transactional store if concurrent processes are supported. Preserve bounded history and cumulative totals.
acceptance: N writers across distinct instances preserve all counts, tokens and costs; history retention limits do not truncate cumulative totals. Document and test the supported cross-process policy.

problem: Web plan saves update JSON without regenerating Markdown, and Web refine saves JSON without refreshing the texts/scripts sidecars. Files representing the same artifact can disagree.
evidence: Python R13: plan PUT changes day_title in JSON while the old Markdown remains unchanged. R03 also observes no TXT generated by successful texts refinement.
recommendation: Centralize canonical artifact persistence and derived rendering, or generate sidecars on explicit export from canonical JSON. Ensure version-safe updates and report/recover failed derivative generation.
acceptance: After plan/texts/scripts saves and refinement, any advertised MD/TXT contains the current canonical content. Conflict/error paths preserve user content and cannot publish derivatives for another revision.

problem: main.py check requires an API key for every bound provider, including keyless Ollama configurations that the provider implementation supports.
evidence: Python R14: with all other checks patched healthy, one local Ollama task with no key produces exit code 1. The user's current cloud/local configuration check separately passes.
recommendation: Share capability/type-aware credential validation with provider construction and doctor readiness rather than imposing a universal key requirement.
acceptance: Valid keyless Ollama bindings pass check; missing credentials for providers requiring them still fail with task/provider-specific guidance; mixed provider configs behave consistently.

problem: Compression groups records by full source path but VideoIndex.write names each index using source_stem alone. Two distinct same-basename sources overwrite one .vindex even though their compressed files have distinct numeric slots.
evidence: Python R15: _write_vindex receives camera-a/shared.mp4 and camera-b/shared.mp4; shared.vindex retains only camera-b and 002_shared.mp4. .vmeta still exists as an independent identity source, so this is not a claim that every downstream operation misidentifies media.
recommendation: Use a stable disambiguated source identity for new index storage and resolve it through shared MediaIdentity helpers; keep legacy stem-index reads with explicit ambiguity handling.
acceptance: Two or more same-basename sources retain separate complete indexes across compress, reindex, verify and single-file analysis; ambiguous legacy lookup never selects another source silently.
dependency: Coordinate with R01 and legacy compatibility

problem: VideoMeta and VideoIndex truncate source modification time to integer seconds and rely on size. Equal-length changes within one second remain reusable despite a changed source timestamp/content.
evidence: Python R16: rewrite a six-byte source and move mtime from .1 to .9 seconds in the same second; VideoMeta.is_stale(source,target) remains false.
recommendation: Version source freshness metadata with mtime_ns and size, and define a stronger content-signature option for workflows preserving timestamps. Retain safe reads for legacy second-resolution fields.
acceptance: Same-size sub-second edits invalidate metadata and reuse. Legacy metadata migration/regeneration is deterministic. Document that preserved timestamps require a content signature and that sampling is not a full integrity hash.

problem: Direct video URLs carry the project name but omit the selected project_dir, although normal API calls support that unambiguous selector. Same-name registered projects therefore fail playback resolution with 409.
evidence: Frontend R17 confirms the selected directory is absent from the player URL. Static backend review confirms duplicate names are deliberately rejected with 409, rather than silently choosing a project.
recommendation: Extend and use the shared media URL builder to propagate canonical project directory identity consistently across player, preloader and cut preview, preserving auth and media parameters.
acceptance: Two registered projects with the same name each play their selected original/compressed/cut media. Player and preloader URLs agree on directory, token, absolute source, day and revision parameters.
dependency: Custom compressed directories also require R07

problem: Typecheck includes only 10 of 81 production JS entry files and uses checkJs=false/strict=false. A green typecheck provides limited assurance for the mutable editor/navigation surfaces.
evidence: Tracked-file inventory counts 81 production JS files; tsconfig explicitly lists 10. Imports may expand the compiler graph, so 10 is the explicit entry count, not an exact graph coverage percentage.
recommendation: Expand @ts-check/JSDoc incrementally around editor state, API responses and async identity/revision contracts; add modules to the checked set without broad any suppression.
acceptance: Core state/save/navigation/refine modules join typecheck and intentional wrong entity/version assignments fail a compiler fixture or documented local check.
dependency: Supports R04-R06; do not duplicate historical OPT-022

problem: Artifact stems incorporate generated titles; title changes increase matching complexity and can leave parallel historical files across analysis/scripts/labels/covers.
evidence: _build_stem uses index plus sanitized title. This is a migration/maintenance risk, not a newly reproduced data-loss incident.
recommendation: Define stable artifact IDs derived from MediaIdentity and keep titles as display metadata; plan backwards-compatible lookup and explicit orphan reporting before changing names.
acceptance: Retitling a clip does not create a second active artifact identity; old title-based files remain readable; migration is reversible and never deletes user-edited files silently.
dependency: Align with R15; do not duplicate historical OPT-023

problem: Frontend global thresholds are far below current coverage, while important editor/viewer paths remain weakly exercised. Happy-path tests miss response reordering and edit-during-save behavior.
evidence: 951 passing tests; statement/branch coverage 61.04%/55.19%; editor-plan 19.79%/14.50%, viewer 38.28%/30.87%. Gates are 25% statements and 22% branches.
recommendation: Add meaningful delayed-response, cross-project and dirty-revision tests; set achievable per-module ratchets for core workflows and a small real-browser scenario suite.
acceptance: R04-R06/R17 fail before fixes and pass after fixes in normal CI. Core workflow coverage ratchets prevent regressions without arbitrary 100% targets; at least one browser flow exercises real routing and editing.

problem: Release builds install unpinned build/GUI dependencies; macOS uses requirements.txt rather than a platform lock. The macOS installer is explicitly pinned to Python 3.11.9. Reproducing the exact shipped dependency set is difficult.
evidence: Workflow text installs pyinstaller/pywebview/platform dependencies without a complete platform build lock. Existing attestations and vulnerability CI are strengths; no new vulnerability or failing release is asserted.
recommendation: Maintain per-platform runtime/build constraints and generate manifests/SBOM from each resolved bundle. Plan a tested runtime migration instead of indefinitely freezing the installer patch level.
acceptance: Windows/macOS builds record all resolved runtime/build versions, verify lock consistency and publish matching artifact-derived manifests. Runtime migration passes native startup/media/dialog checks on both platforms.
dependency: Release environment required; no release triggered by this review

problem: Unit/integration success and a real-ffmpeg fake-provider smoke do not establish real AI output fidelity, browser media behavior or actual JianYing import compatibility.
evidence: This review did not invoke billable providers, open desktop GUI, build packages or import a draft in JianYing. Existing local evaluation fixtures are not evidence for all those boundaries.
recommendation: Keep a small consented media corpus and a versioned acceptance checklist covering AI temporal accuracy, ASR language/noise, browser preview, subtitles, original offsets and manual import.
acceptance: Record fixture, provider/model, app/browser/OS versions and observed results; require human checks of identity, chronology, hallucinations and editability. Billable tests remain explicitly opt-in.

problem: Large orchestration modules and private cross-layer helper imports make cache, persistence and identity contracts easy to reimplement inconsistently.
evidence: Line counts including comments/blanks: 2109, 1664, 1155, 1096 and 1011 respectively. Size alone is not a defect; R01/R07/R13 demonstrate concrete duplicated-policy costs.
recommendation: Extract narrow artifact-resolution/persistence and cache-policy services as fixes require them. Keep CLI/Web adapters thin and avoid a broad rewrite or a single universal manager.
acceptance: Shared services own the relevant contract; preview/runtime and producer/consumer tests use production entry points. Public behavior and legacy reads stay compatible with full relevant suites green.
dependency: Follow functional fixes; avoid independent speculative refactor

problem: ConfigCache describes LRU eviction but cache hits do not refresh insertion order, so eviction follows insertion order for unchanged entries.
evidence: Static inspection: hit returns the cached copy directly; capacity eviction removes next(iter(_cache)). No measured user-visible latency regression is claimed.
recommendation: Either implement recency ordering under the existing lock or document FIFO deliberately; keep per-key synchronization valid during eviction/invalidation.
acceptance: With capacity 2 and access A,B,A,C, the documented policy evicts the expected key; concurrent eviction and reload preserve one coherent result per key.

status: Open; static; narrower than historical OPT-024
problem: Pipeline processed counts are inferred from return shape: integer 0 counts as one processed item, None as zero, and a multi-day mapping as one. warning_count starts at zero without a common warning aggregation contract.
evidence: Static result adapter inspection. Existing failure-code propagation and historical OPT-024 satisfaction are not disputed; this recommendation concerns the accuracy and units of summary metrics.
recommendation: Introduce an internal normalized step outcome for counts/skips/warnings while preserving documented public task returns; label units for clip/day/project results.
acceptance: Disabled transcription reports zero actual work, labels report actual file counts, multi-day planning reports day counts, and warning totals reflect emitted structured warnings without changing failure semantics.
dependency: No UI reinterpretation of historical processing matrices

problem: Operational references retain instructions contradicted by current code: loader-time default injection and Gemini upload deletion. A future maintainer could reintroduce already-fixed behavior.
evidence: Maintenance instructions say missing dataclass defaults are injected; current loader/tracker say reads preserve existing config. Gotchas says uploads are not deleted; current provider has cleanup paths.
recommendation: Reconcile active instructions and mark historical gotchas as historical with verification links. Keep current invariants in one authoritative convention reference.
acceptance: Active docs agree on read-only loading and upload cleanup; each historical warning states whether it still applies. Documentation link checks and git diff --check pass.

problem: No new scale benchmark was run for many clips, long videos, concurrent projects, retained task history or repeated waveform requests. Per-submission task threads and filesystem scans warrant measured capacity limits.
evidence: Static thread-per-submission implementation plus inventory/cache reads; no resource-exhaustion incident, memory leak or throughput number was established in this review.
recommendation: Measure representative project sizes and queue bursts, then add bounded admission/workers or scan/index improvements only where the results justify them.
acceptance: Publish workload definitions, cold/warm latency, peak threads/RSS and cancellation response. The chosen limit rejects or queues excess work predictably without blocking UI health/SSE traffic.
